title: Regular singular partitive: -a/-ä
summary: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.
Add -a to these words with a, o or u. Use -ä with ä, ö or y, or only neutral e/i. Keep the final vowel. In kuppi, keep strong pp; the partitive does not use the weak stem kupi-.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Keep talo and add -a: talo + a = taloa.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “house”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Add -a to auto: autoa. The ending is selected from the word’s back vowels.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “car”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep lelu and add -a because u is a back vowel: lelua.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “toy”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep pallo unchanged and add -a: palloa.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “ball”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
This i-word keeps i: kahvi + a = kahvia. The back vowel a determines the ending.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “coffee”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep the final ä and add another ä: leipä + ä = leipää.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “bread”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep strong pp and the final i: kuppi + a = kuppia.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “cup”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Front vowels y and ä select -ä: kynä + ä = kynää.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “pen”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not drop the existing final vowel when adding another one.
Choose harmony from the whole word. Neutral e/i do not override a, o or u.
Keep the strong consonants in kuppia.
